title: How Much Fiber in Black Beans? 15g per Cup
description: Black Beans: about 15 g of fiber per 1 cup, cooked (53% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in black beans?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Beans, black, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

intro: Black beans rank #5 of 10 beans and legumes on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in black beans by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in black beans?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists beans, black, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt at 8.7 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup, cooked; 172 g) therefore has about 15 g of fiber and 227 calories. That is 53% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 60% of a 25 g day and 39% of a 38 g day.

Black beans are one of the easiest ways to move a day’s fiber total: one cooked cup covers more than half of a 25 g target on its own. The same cup also brings roughly 15 g of protein, which is why beans anchor so many filling, high-fiber meals.

sections.heading: Canned vs home-cooked black beans
paragraphs: Beans cooked from dry and drained canned beans land in a similar range per cup; the bigger variable is how much you actually eat. Canned labels usually list a 1/2 cup serving with its weight in grams, so compare the gram weight rather than the number on the front of the can.
Rinsing canned beans lowers the sodium from the canning liquid. The fiber is in the bean itself, so rinsing does not wash it away.

sections.heading: How black beans compare with other beans and legumes
paragraphs: Of the 10 beans and legumes on this site, black beans rank #5 for fiber per typical serving and #4 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 6.6 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [pinto beans](/fiber-in-pinto-beans) at 15.4 g (1 cup, cooked); [lentils](/fiber-in-lentils) at 15.6 g (1 cup, cooked); [split peas](/fiber-in-split-peas) at 16.3 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), black beans are #16 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding black beans to your day
paragraphs: Half a cup folded into a burrito bowl, a scoop on a salad, or a bean-and-corn salsa adds 7–8 g without much effort. If beans are new to you, start with a quarter cup and build up over a couple of weeks.

Example: 1 cup black beans, 1 cup brown rice, 1/2 avocado. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 23.2 g of fiber, with 15 g from the black beans. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of black beans?
faqs.a: 8.7 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Beans, black, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in black beans (1/2 cup, cooked)?
faqs.a: About 7.5 g, for 86 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

They can, especially if you rarely eat beans. Beans contain fermentable carbohydrates (galacto-oligosaccharides) that gut bacteria break down. Starting with 1/4 to 1/2 cup, rinsing canned beans, and increasing over a few weeks usually helps. Persistent symptoms are worth raising with a clinician.

faqs.q: Black beans or pinto beans: which has more fiber?
faqs.a: They are close. Cooked black beans are about 15 g (1 cup, cooked) and cooked pinto beans are about 15.4 g (1 cup, cooked). Pick the one you will eat more often.
